_comment: Provenance for the ambience loops that are NOT committed as audio in this
directory. tools/fetch-sources.sh reads this file, downloads each original
from Freesound, checks it against sha256, and cuts the window named in
'trim' -- which is what tools/process-audio.sh then consumes.
Committing the manifest rather than the audio keeps ~26MB of FLAC out of
the repository. The cost is that reproducing the sources needs network
access AND Freesound OAuth2 credentials, because Freesound serves original
files only to authenticated clients. See audio-src/README.md.
The five pre-existing loops (rain, fireplace, forest, ocean, cave) and
timer_chime are committed as .ogg in this directory instead; they predate
this manifest and their originals are no longer retrievable.
'trim.start' was chosen by tools/select-window.py, not by hand: it picks
the least-varying window that also begins and ends quietly, because the
pipeline crossfades the tail over the head.

sounds.name: stream_loop
sounds.title: Stream Wyre forest 8.1.14.flac
sounds.note: Chosen window wanders only 0.64dB with -28.1dB rumble.

sounds.name: crickets_loop
sounds.title: AMB_Rural_Summer_Night.wav
sounds.note: Steadiest of the whole shortlist: 0.61dB wander, -31.5dB rumble.

sounds.name: wind_loop
sounds.title: Howling Wind
sounds.note: Source is only 60s, so there is barely a window to choose. -23.6dB rumble is real wind energy rather than mic handling, so it is left in.

sounds.name: birds_loop
sounds.title: Bird Park Ambience
sounds.note: The only new source needing a high-pass. Its sub-80Hz share is -10.0dB, an order of magnitude above every other new source -- and birds do not produce bass, so that is mic wind or distant traffic. Same defect and same 80Hz fix as forest_loop.

sounds.name: cafe_loop
sounds.title: Crowd at Cafeteria
sounds.note: Chosen over higher-rated cafe recordings because those carried 13.7dB spikes from a milk frother, which would punch through on every pass of the loop.

synthesised.name: white_noise_loop
synthesised.note: 96k rather than 128k: measured bandwidth is 20.3kHz at both, and coding artefacts on noise are themselves noise. Saves 113KB.
